name: Las Américas International Airport
before:
Santo Domingo's international airport, at Punta Caucedo between the capital and Boca Chica. It is second busiest in the Dominican Republic after Punta Cana, handling 5.49 million passengers in 2023, and one of the largest airports in the Caribbean.

It is also the busiest cargo hub in the Caribbean and Central America, moving 355 million pounds of freight in 2019.

The runway is the largest in the country at 3,355 metres and takes a 747, which is why long haul, mid haul and short haul aircraft all come in here. Santo Domingo's other airport, La Isabela, only takes small aircraft.

There are two terminals with nine gates between them, plus a remote stand. Terminal B has a Copa Club run jointly by Copa Airlines and United. Between 68 and 84 flights come and go on an average day, and JetBlue is the largest airline.

A 250 million dollar terminal expansion began in June 2025 and is due at the end of 2028.
after:
Santo Domingo's international airport, between the capital and Boca Chica. It is the second busiest in the Dominican Republic after Punta Cana: the civil aviation board counted about 5.2 million international passengers in 2025, 6 per cent fewer than in 2024.

The main runway, at 3,353 metres, is the longest in the country. On the board's figures, its busiest routes in 2025 were to New York, Miami and Madrid. Santo Domingo's other airport, La Isabela, is much smaller.

There are two terminals, and Terminal B has a Copa Club. JetBlue is the largest airline.

Aerodom, which runs the airport, began work on a new 250 million dollar passenger terminal in June 2025, due to be finished in 2028. The airport says the building work is under way and has opened remote car parks with a free shuttle bus in the meantime.

claims.note: Was 'handling 5.49 million passengers in 2023' (Wikipedia's lead). A passenger total replaces a passenger total. JAC's report covers international commercial traffic, so the text says international passengers; Las Américas has almost no domestic scheduled flying. JAC's 2024 figure, 5,534,893, is exactly the 2024 total in Wikipedia's infobox (sourced there to the Central Bank), a good cross-check, but no second source for 2025 was read, so the 2025 figure is attributed. JAC puts the fall mainly down to Arajet moving a large part of its flying to Punta Cana.

OurAirports' runway data for every Dominican airport with scheduled flights puts it first, ahead of Punta Cana's two 3,100 m runways. 'Main' because OurAirports also lists a second, unlit strip, 18/36 (2,991 m), which Wikipedia describes as the parallel taxiway used as a runway during the 2008 resurfacing. Review (23 Sep): the helper's ranking covers airports with scheduled service only; re-run over every Dominican airport in OurAirports (runways.csv, open runways), Las Américas' 11,000 ft runway is still the longest.

claims.claim: new 250 million dollar terminal begun June 2025, due in 2028
claims.inAfter: began work on a new 250 million dollar passenger terminal in June 2025, due to be finished in 2028
claims.note: Was 'A 250 million dollar terminal expansion began in June 2025 and is due at the end of 2028'. Hoy carries Aerodom's announcement of 3 June 2025: demolitions begun, US$250 million, a terminal for 4 million passengers a year, building to finish in 2028 and to run alongside the existing terminal. Wikipedia says the end of 2028; the announcement says only 2028, so the text says 2028. Both sources date from or rest on June 2025; the airport's live page (next claim) shows the work is still going on.
